ArchitectureNotes.objective: Keep the upstream API contract local, generated, and reproducible while exposing ergonomic project workflows through env-safe auth, ephemeral SID context, and stable aliases.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: Do not design opinionated task workflows until project read flows, reference resolution, and write-safe transport behavior are proven.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Keep handwritten runtime logic thin so upstream API drift is absorbed by the snapshot and generation pipeline rather than duplicated request code.

DF-SYNC-SPEC.NAME: Refresh OpenAPI Snapshot
DF-SYNC-SPEC.step-1: Fetch `swagger-ui-init.js` from the upstream Singularity Swagger UI endpoint.
DF-SYNC-SPEC.step-2: Extract the embedded `swaggerDoc` payload from the JavaScript bootstrap source.
DF-SYNC-SPEC.step-3: Serialize the extracted document into `openapi/swagger.json` with stable formatting.
DF-SYNC-SPEC.evidence: `openapi/swagger.json` contains a valid `openapi` field and matches the latest published Swagger UI payload.

DF-GENERATE-SDK.NAME: Generate Local SDK
DF-GENERATE-SDK.TRIGGER: Developer runs bun run codegen or bun run api:refresh
DF-GENERATE-SDK.evidence: The generation command finishes successfully and outputs a typed client tree under `src/api/generated`.

DF-AUTH-LOGIN.NAME: Store Local Auth Token
DF-AUTH-LOGIN.step-1: The command reads a token from `--token` or an interactive prompt.
DF-AUTH-LOGIN.step-2: The auth runtime optionally validates the token by probing the API.
DF-AUTH-LOGIN.step-3: The config module persists the token to config storage.
DF-AUTH-LOGIN.evidence: The token is saved locally with secure permissions and `singu auth status` reports a file-backed token when no env override exists.

DF-AUTH-STATUS.NAME: Inspect Current Auth State
DF-AUTH-STATUS.step-1: The auth runtime resolves env-first token state from the shell and config file.
DF-AUTH-STATUS.step-2: The command renders token source, config path, and masked token information.
DF-AUTH-STATUS.step-3: With `--check`, the auth runtime validates the active token against the API.
DF-AUTH-STATUS.evidence: The command clearly reports whether auth is missing, env-backed, file-backed, valid, or invalid without leaking the raw token.

DF-PROJECT-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.NAME: List Projects And Save SID Context
DF-PROJECT-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.step-1: The command resolves the active token and creates an authorized generated-client wrapper.
DF-PROJECT-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.step-2: The command calls `/v2/project` with the selected pagination and archive flags.
DF-PROJECT-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.step-3: The command prints rows with numeric SIDs and saves the current account-scoped SID map into cache storage.
DF-PROJECT-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.evidence: The user can immediately run `singu project get 1` and resolve the same project from the saved cache.

DF-PROJECT-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.NAME: Resolve Project Reference
DF-PROJECT-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.TRIGGER: User passes a raw id, SID, or alias to a project command
DF-PROJECT-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.step-1: The resolver reads the active auth context and current account fingerprint.
DF-PROJECT-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.step-2: The resolver checks `@alias` references against config-backed aliases and numeric references against cache-backed SID context.
DF-PROJECT-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.step-3: The resolver falls back to explicit raw ids and returns the final Singularity project id plus reference metadata.
DF-PROJECT-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.evidence: The same target project can be addressed through raw id, SID, or alias depending on local context.

DF-PROJECT-ALIAS-SET.NAME: Persist Project Alias
DF-PROJECT-ALIAS-SET.TRIGGER: User runs singu project alias set alias-name project-reference
DF-PROJECT-ALIAS-SET.step-1: The command resolves the provided project reference into a raw project id.
DF-PROJECT-ALIAS-SET.step-2: The alias store validates and normalizes the alias name.
DF-PROJECT-ALIAS-SET.step-3: The alias store persists the alias under the active account fingerprint inside config storage.
DF-PROJECT-ALIAS-SET.evidence: The user can later run `singu project get @name` even after the last-list cache changes.

DF-PROJECT-GET.NAME: Fetch Single Project
DF-PROJECT-GET.TRIGGER: User runs singu project get project-reference
DF-PROJECT-GET.step-1: The command resolves the input reference through the project reference resolver.
DF-PROJECT-GET.step-2: The command calls `/v2/project/:id` through the authorized HTTP wrapper and generated client.
DF-PROJECT-GET.step-3: The command renders human-readable project fields or raw JSON output.
DF-PROJECT-GET.evidence: `project get` succeeds for references produced by `project list`, `project alias set`, or direct raw ids.

DF-TASK-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.NAME: List Tasks And Save SID Context
DF-TASK-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.step-1: The command resolves the active token and creates an authorized generated-client wrapper.
DF-TASK-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.step-2: The command calls `/v2/task` with the selected server-side filters and optional project reference.
DF-TASK-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.step-3: The command applies client-side default actionable grouping or inbox filtering when `--all` is not selected.
DF-TASK-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.step-4: The command prints rows with numeric SIDs and saves the current account-scoped SID map into cache storage.
DF-TASK-LIST-SAVE-CONTEXT.evidence: The user can immediately run `singu task get 1` and resolve the same visible task from the saved cache.

DF-TASK-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.NAME: Resolve Task Reference
DF-TASK-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.TRIGGER: User passes a raw id, SID, or alias to a task command
DF-TASK-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.step-1: The resolver reads the active auth context and current account fingerprint.
DF-TASK-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.step-2: The resolver checks `@alias` references against config-backed aliases and numeric references against cache-backed SID context.
DF-TASK-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.step-3: The resolver falls back to explicit raw ids and returns the final Singularity task id plus reference metadata.
DF-TASK-RESOLVE-REFERENCE.evidence: The same target task can be addressed through raw id, SID, or alias depending on local context.

DF-TASK-ALIAS-SET.NAME: Persist Task Alias
DF-TASK-ALIAS-SET.TRIGGER: User runs singu task alias set alias-name task-reference
DF-TASK-ALIAS-SET.step-1: The command resolves the provided task reference into a raw task id.
DF-TASK-ALIAS-SET.step-2: The alias store validates and normalizes the alias name.
DF-TASK-ALIAS-SET.step-3: The alias store persists the alias under the active account fingerprint inside config storage.
DF-TASK-ALIAS-SET.evidence: The user can later run `singu task get @name` even after the last-list cache changes.

DF-TASK-GET.NAME: Fetch Single Task
DF-TASK-GET.TRIGGER: User runs singu task get task-reference
DF-TASK-GET.step-1: The command resolves the input reference through the task reference resolver.
DF-TASK-GET.step-2: The command calls `/v2/task/:id` through the authorized HTTP wrapper and generated client.
DF-TASK-GET.step-3: The command renders human-readable task fields or raw JSON output.
DF-TASK-GET.evidence: `task get` succeeds for references produced by `task list`, `task alias set`, or direct raw ids.

DF-TASK-CHECK-UPDATE.NAME: Mark Task Done Or Reopen
DF-TASK-CHECK-UPDATE.TRIGGER: User runs singu task do task-reference or singu task undo task-reference
DF-TASK-CHECK-UPDATE.step-1: The command resolves the input reference through the task reference resolver.
DF-TASK-CHECK-UPDATE.step-2: The command fetches the current task state to avoid redundant updates.
DF-TASK-CHECK-UPDATE.step-3: The command sends a minimal PATCH update that changes `checked` to done or open.
DF-TASK-CHECK-UPDATE.step-4: The command prints the result and reminds the user to refresh list-based SIDs.
DF-TASK-CHECK-UPDATE.evidence: `task do` and `task undo` work with raw ids, SIDs, and aliases and avoid extra updates when the task is already in the target state.

DF-TASK-ADD.NAME: Create Task
DF-TASK-ADD.TRIGGER: User runs singu task add title
DF-TASK-ADD.step-1: The command resolves the active token and optional project reference.
DF-TASK-ADD.step-2: The command creates a task from the provided title and optional project assignment.
DF-TASK-ADD.step-3: The command prints the created task id and current project assignment.
DF-TASK-ADD.evidence: `task add` can create inbox tasks and project-bound tasks without manual JSON payloads.

DF-TASK-MOVE.NAME: Move Task
DF-TASK-MOVE.TRIGGER: User runs singu task move task-reference
DF-TASK-MOVE.step-1: The command resolves the target task reference.
DF-TASK-MOVE.step-2: The command resolves the destination project reference or accepts `--inbox` as a clear-project action.
DF-TASK-MOVE.step-3: The command patches the task with the new project assignment and reports the result.
DF-TASK-MOVE.evidence: `task move` can move tasks into a project or back to inbox through project references.

DF-TASK-SCHEDULE.NAME: Schedule Task
DF-TASK-SCHEDULE.TRIGGER: User runs singu task schedule task-reference
DF-TASK-SCHEDULE.step-1: The command resolves the target task reference.
DF-TASK-SCHEDULE.step-2: The command parses `--start` and optional `--deadline` inputs into stable task payload values.
DF-TASK-SCHEDULE.step-3: The command patches the task scheduling fields and reports the result.
DF-TASK-SCHEDULE.evidence: `task schedule` accepts `now`, `today`, `tomorrow`, dates, and datetimes without manual payload construction.

DF-TASK-EDIT.NAME: Edit Task
DF-TASK-EDIT.TRIGGER: User runs singu task edit task-reference
DF-TASK-EDIT.step-1: The command resolves the target task reference.
DF-TASK-EDIT.step-2: The command validates a new title from CLI input.
DF-TASK-EDIT.step-3: The command patches the task and reports the updated title and id.
DF-TASK-EDIT.evidence: `task edit` can rename tasks through raw ids, SIDs, and aliases.

DF-TASK-UNSCHEDULE.NAME: Unschedule Task
DF-TASK-UNSCHEDULE.TRIGGER: User runs singu task unschedule task-reference
DF-TASK-UNSCHEDULE.step-1: The command resolves the target task reference.
DF-TASK-UNSCHEDULE.step-2: The command clears start and deadline values and resets time-based scheduling flags.
DF-TASK-UNSCHEDULE.step-3: The command reports the updated scheduling state.
DF-TASK-UNSCHEDULE.evidence: `task unschedule` removes schedule metadata without requiring manual payload construction.

DF-TASK-REMOVE.NAME: Remove Task
DF-TASK-REMOVE.TRIGGER: User runs singu task rm task-reference
DF-TASK-REMOVE.step-1: The command resolves the target task reference.
DF-TASK-REMOVE.step-2: The command calls the generated delete endpoint for the resolved raw task id.
DF-TASK-REMOVE.step-3: The command reports success and reminds the user to refresh short ids.
DF-TASK-REMOVE.evidence: `task rm` deletes tasks through raw ids, SIDs, and aliases.

DF-BLOCK-CREATE.NAME: Create Focus Block
DF-BLOCK-CREATE.TRIGGER: User runs singu block duration title
DF-BLOCK-CREATE.step-1: The command parses the duration input and resolves an optional project reference.
DF-BLOCK-CREATE.step-2: The command creates a task with `start` set to now and `deadline` derived from the parsed duration.
DF-BLOCK-CREATE.step-3: The command sets `useTime` and `timeLength` so the created task behaves like a real scheduled block.
DF-BLOCK-CREATE.evidence: `block` creates a scheduled task without requiring a separate add plus schedule flow.

Phase-1.name: Foundation
Phase-1.goal: Establish local snapshot refresh, code generation, and a minimal CLI entry point.
Phase-1.step-1: Implement the OpenAPI snapshot refresh command.
Phase-1.step-2: Configure Kubb against the local snapshot and generated SDK output path.
Phase-1.step-3: Create the top-level citty entry point and binary build script.

Phase-2.name: Runtime Core
Phase-2.goal: Add storage resolution, config handling, auth behavior, generated client consumption, and normalized transport errors.
Phase-2.step-1: Implement `SINGU_HOME` override and XDG-first storage path resolution.
Phase-2.step-2: Implement local config and token persistence on top of storage paths.
Phase-2.step-3: Implement env-first auth state resolution, token validation, and account fingerprints.
Phase-2.step-4: Generate and validate the local SDK from the stored snapshot.
Phase-2.step-5: Wrap generated clients with authorized transport and stable non-2xx errors.

Phase-3.name: Project Read UX
Phase-3.goal: Ship the auth command set and the first project read flows with ergonomic reference resolution.
Phase-3.step-1: Implement `auth login`, `auth status`, and `auth logout` on top of the auth runtime.
Phase-3.step-2: Implement last-list SID cache persistence in cache storage.
Phase-3.step-3: Implement account-scoped alias persistence in config storage.
Phase-3.step-4: Resolve raw ids, SIDs, and aliases into project ids.
Phase-3.step-5: Implement `project list` and `project get` with reference-aware UX.
Phase-3.step-6: Implement `project alias set`, `project alias list`, and `project alias remove`.

Phase-4.name: Project Write UX
Phase-4.goal: Build create, update, and delete flows on top of the stabilized reference and auth layers.

Phase-5.name: Task Read UX
Phase-5.goal: Ship task read flows with the same SID and alias ergonomics already used for projects.
Phase-5.step-1: Implement last-list SID cache persistence for tasks.
Phase-5.step-2: Implement account-scoped task alias persistence in shared config storage.
Phase-5.step-3: Resolve raw ids, SIDs, and aliases into task ids.
Phase-5.step-4: Implement `task list` and `task get` with reference-aware UX.
Phase-5.step-5: Implement `task alias set`, `task alias list`, and `task alias remove`.

Phase-6.name: Task Action UX
Phase-6.goal: Add the first task state-changing commands on top of the stabilized task reference layer.

Phase-7.name: Task Write UX
Phase-7.goal: Add task creation, triage, scheduling, and focus-block capture workflows.
Phase-7.step-1: Implement duration and schedule input parsing helpers.
Phase-7.step-2: Implement `task add`, `task edit`, `task move`, `task schedule`, `task unschedule`, and `task rm`.
Phase-7.step-3: Implement top-level `block` for immediate scheduled task creation.

ExecutionPolicy.worker-owns: Only approved source files, command modules, and module-local tests inside the active execution scope.
